extracted.intended_audience: People who contribute/upload b-files or other files to the On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences (OEIS); registered OEIS contributors
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and uploading b-files (and other files) to an OEIS sequence entry, including format, naming, upload/linking, size/encoding limits, provenance and licensing requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: b-file line format
rubrics_metrics.description: Each line is a pair "n a(n)" with n first, a single space, then a(n). No commas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One line per entry; even if a(n) is very large it should remain on a single line. If possible use spaces rather than tabs to separate the two numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: starting offset
rubrics_metrics.description: The values of n should start with the offset of the sequence (the first number in the Offset line in the entry).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The offset in the b-file must agree with that of the sequence; if the offset is wrong in the sequence it must be corrected before the b-file can be uploaded.

rubrics_metrics.name: consecutive n values (no gaps)
rubrics_metrics.description: The b-file cannot contain gaps; the values of n must be consecutive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there are missing entries use an a-file instead (in an a-file you can put question marks for the missing entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: comment lines ignored
rubrics_metrics.description: Lines beginning with # are comment lines and are ignored by the system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can put the computing program at the head of the b-file with a # at the start of each line so those lines are ignored by commands that parse the b-file.

rubrics_metrics.name: blank lines ignored and file must end with blank line
rubrics_metrics.description: Blank lines are ignored. YOU SHOULD END THE FILE WITH A BLANK LINE. OTHERWISE THE LAST DATA LINE MAY BE IGNORED.

rubrics_metrics.name: file encoding and BOM
rubrics_metrics.description: The b-file should be in plain ASCII (not UTF-8, say).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The b files have a strict format; byte order marks are not allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: maximum digits per term
rubrics_metrics.description: a(n) should not have more than about 1000 digits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some of the OEIS programs will fail if entries exceed ~1000 digits.

rubrics_metrics.name: file size limit
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a limit of about 10 megabytes on the size of a b-file that can be uploaded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your file exceeds that there will be no warning, but the file will be broken. Always check the file was uploaded correctly (e.g., click the link and inspect the terms). To upload a larger b-file, ask [email protected] for help.

rubrics_metrics.name: filename convention for b-files
rubrics_metrics.description: The name of the b-file for A123456 would be b123456.txt; b-files are always bNNNNNN.txt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use lower-case b followed by the six-digit sequence number and .txt.

rubrics_metrics.name: filename convention for other files
rubrics_metrics.description: Files associated with sequence ANNNNNN should always start with aNNNNNN (with a lower-case a); other files are named aNNNNNN.<ext> (or get .txt appended).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the uploaded filename doesn't have one of the allowed text extensions it gets .txt added (e.g., prog.c will be saved as aNNNNNN.c.txt).

rubrics_metrics.name: allowed text and binary extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowed file extensions for text files: .eps, .nb, .ps, .rtf, .svg, .tex, .txt. For binary files the allowed formats are: pdf, gif, jpg, png, tiff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any text file is okay; the listed extensions only affect whether .txt gets added automatically. Typical uploaded files include program source (a123456.map.txt), large tables, or drawings (aNNNNNN.jpg).

rubrics_metrics.name: link creation is required
rubrics_metrics.description: When you upload a b-file (or other file), you must also create a link to it which will be added to the sequence entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you don't create a link, no one will ever see the b-file. When you upload the file you will see a template for the link that you can edit; the MIN and MAX values will be automatically filled in by the system.

rubrics_metrics.name: b-file must agree with existing Data
rubrics_metrics.description: You will be warned if the b-file does not agree with the existing terms in the Data section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there was an error in the sequence, it must be corrected before a b-file can be uploaded.

rubrics_metrics.name: triangle flattening guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The b-file for a triangle of numbers is obtained by 'flattening' the triangle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See example b-files such as Pascal's triangle (A007318) for the flattening format; when uploading indicate in the link text which rows/ranges are included.

rubrics_metrics.name: provenance and authorship when extending files
rubrics_metrics.description: If you extend a b-file by adding more terms, replace the author's name(s) with your name(s) and after the link add a comment indicating which ranges come from which contributor(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'terms 1..500 from Jon E. Schoenfield, terms 501..1000 from Chai Wah Wu'. This documents provenance so others can verify work.

rubrics_metrics.name: include computation program when possible
rubrics_metrics.description: So others can verify your work, if possible include the program used to compute the b-file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Put the program at the head of the b-file with # at the start of each line, or include it as a separate text file attached to the sequence with a name like a123456_Maple.txt or a234567_Py.txt.

rubrics_metrics.name: login/registration requirement for uploads
rubrics_metrics.description: You must register before you can log in, and you must log in before you can see the 'Edit' tab for a sequence and upload files.

rubrics_metrics.name: editorial/licensing/legal requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Contributions are under The OEIS Contributor's License Agreement and may be edited, altered, or removed by other contributors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit copyrighted work without permission. You are promising that you wrote this yourself, or copied it from a public domain resource, or have the right to submit it. Standards are those of a mathematics reference work; thousands use the database daily—take great care that what you send is absolutely correct.

rubrics_metrics.name: size guidance and editorial discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical b-file sizes: 100, 1000, 10000, 20000 terms are usual; 10000 terms is most common.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Editors-in-Chief have the final say about what size of b-file is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: post-upload verification
rubrics_metrics.description: After uploading, check that the file was uploaded correctly by clicking the link and inspecting the terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There may be no warning if an oversized file is broken; manual verification is necessary.
